headline: 8 token contract addresses catalogued across Sui, Aptos, Solana, and X Layer; Bitcoin chain holds BTC reserves at OKX custody (no on-chain contracts); admin/control addresses not publicly disclosed.

findings.text: D1: Block-explorer search for 'OKX xBTC' on Sui (suiscan.xyz) returned generic page without coin-specific data (JS-rendered). X Layer explorer (oklink.com/x-layer) not directly fetched — addresses sourced from official OKX website table instead. No EVM block-explorer name-tags found for xBTC on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, or other EVM chains. Bitcoin chain has no on-chain smart contracts — reserve BTC is custodied by OKX in an undisclosed Bitcoin address.

D2: Official deployments table found on https://www.okx.com/xbtc#transparency (rendered at https://www.okx.com/en-us/x-rwa). Table lists 8 token contract addresses across Sui, Aptos, Solana, and X Layer. No separate /docs/deployments page exists; the transparency page IS the deployed-contracts reference.

D3: xBTC whitepaper (https://www.okx.com/cdn/oksupport/common/xBTC_Whitepaper.abb0ea55a766e9.pdf) confirms CertiK and MoveBit audited Sui/Aptos contracts; Zellic audits EVM (X Layer) contracts. Audit completed May 19, 2025. CertiK Skynet page (https://skynet.certik.com/projects/okx-web3) confirms 'XBTC (OKX wrapped BTC) - audit' requested 4/28/2025, revised 5/9/2025, with 2 findings (1 centralization acknowledged, 1 informational resolved). Direct PDF URLs for CertiK/MoveBit/Zellic xBTC audit reports not surfaced in this run.

D4: GitHub repo is https://github.com/okx/xAsset (branch xbtc-sui), not the previously referenced okx/xBTC. Repo contains Move.toml, sources/xbtc.move, and deployment scripts for Sui. No hardhat-deploy JSON or broadcast JSON with deployed addresses found in the repo. Commit SHA not pinned (branch HEAD used). Aptos source code also lives in this repo per whitepaper. No deployment artifact files (run-latest.json, deployments.json, etc.) observed.

D5: Protocol.chains = ['Bitcoin'] per DeFiLlama, but actual token deployments are on Sui, Aptos, Solana, and X Layer. Bitcoin chain is the reserve/collateral layer (BTC custodied by OKX), not a smart-contract deployment chain. Each deployed chain has one xBTC token contract listed. Additional X Layer contracts for xETH, xSOL, xBETH, xOKSOL also listed on the official page. On-chain reads for Sui/Aptos/Solana not possible via DeFiPunkd API (chainIds 784, 1, etc. not supported for non-EVM). X Layer not listed in supported DeFiPunkd chainIds.
D6: No factory contracts identified. xBTC is deployed as a single token per chain. No enumeration needed.

D7: Roles documented in whitepaper: TreasuryCap (mint/burn), DenyCapV2 (blacklist/denylist), XBTCReceiver (designated minting receiver, shared object on Sui). On Solana: MintAuthority, FreezeAuthority, UpdateAuthority. All controlled by OKX. Specific holder addresses (EOA or multisig) not disclosed in any fetched source.

D8: All 8 token contract addresses trace to the official OKX website table (https://www.okx.com/en-us/x-rwa). Note: Sui and Aptos addresses are Move object IDs / FA addresses, not EVM 0x addresses; Solana address is a base58 SPL mint; X Layer addresses are EVM 0x addresses. Admin/capability holder addresses not surfaced — recorded in unknowns[].

rationale.verdict: Discovery catalogued 8 token contract addresses across 4 chains (Sui, Aptos, Solana, X Layer) from the official OKX X-RWA page, xBTC whitepaper, GitHub repo, and CertiK Skynet. The DeFiLlama 'Bitcoin' chain classification reflects the BTC reserve custody layer, not a deployment chain. Admin capability-holder addresses (TreasuryCap, DenyCapV2, MintAuthority, FreezeAuthority on each chain) remain undisclosed and are recorded as unknowns for downstream slices.

protocol_metadata.about: OKX xBTC (OKX Wrapped BTC) is a centrally-issued wrapped token backed 1:1 by Bitcoin held in OKX's custody. Users withdraw BTC from their OKX exchange account to receive xBTC on supported blockchains (Sui, Aptos, Solana, X Layer), enabling use in DeFi applications such as lending, borrowing, and liquidity mining. Redemption occurs by depositing xBTC back to an OKX exchange account, which burns the token and releases the equivalent BTC from OKX's reserve address. OKX controls all minting, burning, blacklisting, and pausing capabilities unilaterally; there is no decentralized governance.
